university: University of Texas at San Antonio
notes: Single university-layer document (UTSA Academic Innovation faculty guide, PDF dated January 2025); no school or computing documents found, course layer deferred. Coder A and B alignment: 78 matched units, 3 only-A (all kept), 6 only-B (5 kept, 1 dropped: a resource list of office names). Coder-specific topic labels were normalized to the shared topic vocabulary. Fit notes from both coders were kept and merged. Candidate pattern for review: account-security tips for AI platforms (two-factor authentication) have no type and are coded UNCOVERED; a few units (cache clearing, ethics reflection) fit P50 and P53 only partly.

documents.title: From Imagination to Implementation: Using Generative AI in Teaching and Learning (UTSA faculty GenAI guidelines)
documents.date_or_term: January 2025 (text says created January 2024; reviewed annually)
tiers: authorized only as a virtual learning assistant
documents.summary: A provost-level faculty guide that sets no university-wide rule on student AI use. It tells faculty to state in their syllabus whether AI is encouraged, limited or not allowed, names Microsoft CoPilot as the only approved tool, and advises on privacy, detectors, assessment redesign, research and faculty development.
documents.stance_why: The guide says "Faculty are responsible for their syllabus and courses" and "You always have control over your course", and lists three example statements (AI use "encouraged", "authorized only as a virtual learning assistant", "not authorized"). It sets no university-wide default for student AI use, so the stance is delegates with those three tiers.
